To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the newly revised MNA short form is a valid nutritional tool applicable to geriatrics and includes a "malnouished" category.

1) the original MNA short form (six questions) was validated in a large dataset of 2032 patients; 2) calf circumference was substituted for BMI in the revised MNA short form; and 3) the revised MNA SF has good sensitivity compared to MNA.
the MNA(r) SF, a tool that is used to screen for malnutrition in elderly people, has been revised to include calf circumference (CC).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the best combination of questions from the full Mini Nutritional Assessment (MNA) to form a short form (MNa SF), which can be used as a rapid screening tool for nutritional status in elderly people.
the development and validation of a short form version of the MNA.
the development, validation and application of the MNA SF as a screening tool for the identification of malnutrition in geriatric patients in clinical practice and research settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this revised MNA short form is a valid tool for the nutritional evaluation of older people in clinical practice.
the revised MNA(r) SF is a practical tool for nutritional screening in older persons.

a revised MNA SF using calf circumference instead of BMI, and a three category classification (normal, at risk of malnutrition, malnourished) is a valid nutritional assessment tool in geriatric health care practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the revised MNA SF has the same validity as the original MNA SF, and the revised MNA scoring system is a valid classification system for the MNA SF.
the MNA SF, including calf circumference (CC), is valid for use in nutritional screening in geriatrics.
the revised MNA SF can be considered an acceptable alternative to the full MMA in clinical settings where the MNA cannot be applied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MNA short form is a practical, valid and easy-to-use tool to assess nutritional status in older adults.
a combination of BMI and CC is a valid alternative to the full MAA SF for the identification of malnourished older people.
the MNA SF can be used as a valid screening tool for nutritional status in geriatric populations, even when BMI is not available.
